A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OMG/SOMG research. All pages, mathematical displays, Table 1, algorithms, and appendices are readable, allowing substantive changes to be distinguished from relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports algorithms, theoretical guarantees, and proofs, including its appendices. Table 1 compares theoretical bounds; no original experimental or simulation outcomes are reported.

after.justification: v2 remains theoretical. Its revised proofs and additional discussions introduce no original experimental, simulation, or data-analysis outcomes.

M1.justification: OMG and SOMG retain their main procedures. SOMG's bonus coefficient gains H and regularization-dependent logarithmic factors. The explicit unregularized specialization in v1 Appendix C.6 is removed, while v2 Appendix D.2 sketches an adaptation using general-function uncertainty widths.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or executed evaluation tasks. Appendix D discusses theoretical extensions, not additional tested scenarios.

E2.justification: Neither version reports experimental baseline evaluations. Table 1's changed selection of published theoretical guarantees concerns research positioning rather than evaluated comparator membership.

E3.justification: Neither version reports experimental protocols, data splits, evaluation budgets, or testing procedures. Revised algorithm coefficients and theorem conditions are theoretical changes.

E4.justification: Neither version contains ablations, robustness experiments, sensitivity tests, or empirical case studies. The new appendix material consists of theoretical derivations and discussion.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, or empirical uncertainty estimates. Changes to failure-probability allocation occur within mathematical concentration proofs and are assessed under T1.

E6.justification: No measured numerical results or experimental findings appear in either version. Changes to regret and sample-complexity bounds are theoretical revisions covered under T1.

T1.justification: v1 Lemma C.10 treats a fixed opponent policy; v2 replaces this with an equilibrium-dependent MSE value-function argument and adds superoptimistic covering, KL-identity, and payoff-stability proofs in Lemmas C.11–C.13. Concentration proofs now allocate failure probability across the horizon. Theorem 3.1 adds H/min{1,β} inside logarithms and restricts both guarantees to β>0. The unregularized theorem and supporting proofs in v1 Appendix C.6 are removed. Appendix D.2 adds general-function assumptions and mathematical definitions.

C1.justification: The headline logarithmic-regret and linear-in-1/ε sample-complexity contributions remain. However, the abstract and contribution statements retreat from SOMG's regularization-independent square-root guarantee: v2 allows logarithmic β dependence and withdraws its unregularized Markov-game guarantee.

C2.justification: Sections 3.3 and 4.2 newly explain why changing equilibrium policies complicate covering-number bounds and introduce logarithmic regularization dependence. Appendix D.2 discusses conditions for extending beyond linear approximation. Appendix D.1 expands the already-present single-agent interpretation rather than introducing that reduction.

D1.justification: Explicit SOMG bonus-tuning prescriptions change, and the unregularized projection/bonus prescriptions are removed. A remaining inconsistency affects these instructions: v2 Lemma C.1 includes H inside η1's logarithm, whereas the prescription following Eq. (24) retains the earlier expression. No implementation resources are added.

R1.justification: v2 adds Ye et al. (2023) and removes Boyd and Vandenberghe (2004). Table 1 drops the OMNI-VI and Nash-UCRL theoretical comparisons, although their works remain discussed. Appendix D adds more explicit connections to existing general-function techniques and single-agent bounds.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most prose remain intact. v2 organizes technical challenges into bullets, adds explanatory passages and Appendix D, revises guarantee terminology, and makes localized wording and cross-reference corrections.

P2.justification: Table 1 is reformatted with revised rows and caption, including separate regularized/unregularized matrix-game entries for Yang et al. Algorithm 1 moves from page 8 to page 7. Other changes are principally equation formatting and pagination; neither version contains figures.

improvement.justification: The decisive gain is stronger support for the central Markov-game analysis: v2 replaces v1's fixed-opponent covering argument with arguments accounting for changing equilibrium policies and superoptimistic values. It also exposes additional logarithmic dependencies and withdraws the unregularized guarantee. These changes substantially improve the rigor and calibration of this theoretical paper, despite narrower guarantees and a remaining η1 inconsistency between Eq. (24) and Lemma C.1.
